10→ Grok Build (grok)

**Grok Build** is SpaceXAI's terminal-based AI coding agent. It runs as a full-screen TUI that understands your codebase, edits files, executes shell commands, searches the web, and manages long-running tasks — interactively, headlessly for scripting/CI, or embedded in editors via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). [Installing the released binary](#installing-the-released-binary) · 20→[Building from source](#building-from-source) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Repository layout](#repository-layout) · [Development](#development) · [Contributing](#contributing) · [License](#license) ![Grok Build TUI](https://media.x.ai/v1/website/universe-tui-screenshot-6f7a0837.png) **Learn more about Grok Build at [x.ai/cli](https://x.ai/cli)** 30→ This repository contains the Rust source for the `grok` CLI/TUI and its agent runtime. It is synced periodically from the SpaceXAI monorepo. A small `SOURCE_REV` file at the root records the full monorepo commit SHA for the version of the code present in this tree.
--- 40→ ## Installing the released binary Prebuilt binaries are published for macOS, Linux, and Windows: ```sh curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash # macOS / Linux / Git Bash irm https://x.ai/cli/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell grok --version ``` 50→ See the [changelog](https://x.ai/build/changelog) for the latest fixes, features, and improvements in each release. ## Building from source Requirements: - **Rust** — the toolchain is pinned by [`rust-toolchain.toml`](rust-toolchain.toml); `rustup` installs it automatically on first build. 60→- **[DotSlash](https://dotslash-cli.com)** — required so hermetic tools under [`bin/`](bin/) (notably [`bin/protoc`](bin/protoc)) can download and run. Install it and ensure `dotslash` is on your `PATH` **before** building: ```sh cargo install dotslash # or: prebuilt packages — https://dotslash-cli.com/docs/installation/ /usr/bin/env dotslash --help # sanity check ``` 70→- **protoc** — proto codegen resolves [`bin/protoc`](bin/protoc) via DotSlash, or falls back to a `protoc` on `PATH` / `$PROTOC`. - macOS and Linux are supported build hosts; Windows builds are best-effort and not currently tested from this tree. ```sh cargo run -p xai-grok-pager-bin # build + launch the TUI cargo build -p xai-grok-pager-bin --release # release binary: target/release/xai-grok-pager cargo check -p xai-grok-pager-bin # fast validation ``` 80→ The binary artifact is named `xai-grok-pager`; official installs ship it as `grok`. On first launch it opens your browser to authenticate — see the [authentication guide](crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/02-authentication.md). ## Documentation Full online documentation is available at [docs.x.ai/build/overview](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview). 90→The user guide ships with the pager crate: [`crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/`](crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/) — getting started, keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, configuration, theming, MCP servers, skills, plugins, hooks, headless mode, sandboxing, and more. ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | |------|----------| | `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager-bin` | Composition-root package; builds the `xai-grok-pager` binary | 100→| `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager` | The TUI: scrollback, prompt, modals, rendering | | `crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell` | Agent runtime + leader/stdio/headless entry points | | `crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools` | Tool implementations (terminal, file edit, search, ...) | | `crates/codegen/xai-grok-workspace` | Host filesystem, VCS, execution, checkpoints | | `crates/codegen/...` | The rest of the CLI crate closure (config, MCP, markdown, sandbox, ...) | | `crates/common/`, `crates/build/`, `prod/mc/` | Small shared leaf crates pulled in by the closure | | `third_party/` | Vendored upstream source (Mermaid diagram stack) — see below | > [!IMPORTANT] > The root `Cargo.toml` (workspace members, dependency versions, lints, 110→> profiles) is **generated** — treat it as read-only. Prefer editing per-crate > `Cargo.toml` files. ## Development ```sh cargo check -p # always target specific crates; full-workspace builds are slow cargo test -p xai-grok-config # per-crate tests cargo clippy -p # lint config: clippy.toml at the repo root cargo fmt --all # rustfmt.toml at the repo root 120→``` ## Contributing > [!NOTE] > External contributions are not accepted. See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License First-party code in this repository is licensed under the **Apache License, 130→Version 2.0** — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Third-party and vendored code remains under its original licenses. See: - [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES) — crates.io / git dependencies, bundled UI themes, and **in-tree source ports** (including openai/codex and sst/opencode tool implementations) - [`crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) — crate-local notice for the codex and opencode ports (license texts + Apache §4(b) change notice) 140→- [`third_party/NOTICE`](third_party/NOTICE) — vendored Mermaid-stack index

content.text: I have a good overview from the README. Let me dig a bit more into the architecture - the major crates, SOURCE_REV, rust version, and maybe peek at the shell/pager structure to give a richer conversat...

This is **Grok Build** — SpaceXAI’s terminal coding agent, the thing you’re talking to right now when you run `grok`. The public name of the binary is `grok`; in this tree it still builds as `xai-grok-pager`.

## What it is

A **Rust workspace** for a full-screen TUI that can:

- understand and edit a codebase  
- run shell commands  
- search the web  
- drive long-running tasks  
- run **interactively**, **headlessly** (CI/scripting), or embedded in editors via **ACP** (Agent Client Protocol)

It’s periodically **synced out of the SpaceXAI monorepo**. `SOURCE_REV` pins the monorepo commit this tree came from (`2ec0f0c8…`). History here is thin — essentially “synced from monorepo” / “publish harness and TUI open-source.” Remote is `github.com/xai-org/grok-build`.

**External PRs are not accepted** (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`). License is Apache-2.0 for first-party code.

## Shape of the tree

~**75 workspace crates**, mostly under `crates/codegen/`, with smaller shared pieces in `crates/common/`, proto helpers in `crates/build/`, and a Mermaid diagram stack vendored in `third_party/`.

Rough mental model:

| Layer | Crate(s) | Role |
|--------|-----------|------|
| **Binary entry** | `xai-grok-pager-bin` | Composition root → `xai-grok-pager` / `grok` |
| **TUI** | `xai-grok-pager` (+ `pager-render`, ratatui helpers) | Scrollback, prompt, modals, theming — Elm-style Action → Effect |
| **Agent runtime** | `xai-grok-shell` | Leader/stdio/headless, sessions, sampling, MCP glue |
| **Tools** | `xai-grok-tools` | Shell, files, search, memory, skills, web, MCP `use_tool`, etc. (some ports from Codex / OpenCode, called out in notices) |
| **Workspace host** | `xai-grok-workspace` | FS, VCS, execution, checkpoints |
| **Surrounding product surface** | config, auth, MCP, hooks, plugins, memory, sandbox, telemetry, markdown/mermaid, voice, update, … | Everything that makes a “real” coding agent |

The TUI architecture is deliberately clean: **AppView** (global) / **AgentView** (per session), prompt with `@` file search and `/` slash commands, async effects for ACP and I/O. User-facing docs live in `crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/` (auth, theming, MCP, skills, plan mode, sandbox, subagents, …).

Root `Cargo.toml` is **generated and treated as read-only** — edit per-crate manifests instead. Toolchain is pinned to **Rust 1.92.0**. Builds expect **DotSlash** for hermetic `bin/protoc`.

## How you’d touch it day-to-day

```sh
cargo run -p xai-grok-pager-bin              # build + launch TUI
cargo check -p xai-grok-pager                # prefer package-scoped; full workspace is heavy
cargo test -p xai-grok-config
```

Product docs online: [docs.x.ai/build](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview); install story at [x.ai/cli](https://x.ai/cli).

---

**In short:** this isn’t a small demo CLI — it’s the open-sourced **agent + TUI stack** for Grok Build: a large, modular Rust monorepo slice with a serious terminal UI, tool runtime, workspace isolation, and extension surface (hooks, skills, MCP, plugins). You’re sitting inside the product that this code builds.

Want a deeper tour of a particular layer next — TUI event loop, tool registry, shell/session model, or sandbox/worktree?

**TUI** means **Text User Interface** (sometimes “Terminal User Interface”).

It’s a full-screen app that runs **inside a terminal**, using text, colors, boxes, and keyboard (and sometimes mouse) instead of a native GUI window.

| | GUI | TUI | CLI |
|---|-----|-----|-----|
| **Looks like** | Windows, buttons, mouse | Layout drawn with characters in the terminal | Lines of text + commands |
| **Examples** | VS Code, Finder | `htop`, `vim`, `lazygit`, Grok Build | `ls`, `git status` |

**Grok Build’s TUI** is the interactive full-screen experience: scrollback of the conversation, the prompt at the bottom, modals, status bars, slash-command menus — all rendered in the terminal by crates like `xai-grok-pager` (often with libraries like **ratatui** under the hood).

So when the README says “terminal-based AI coding agent” with a “full-screen TUI,” it means: not just a one-shot CLI that prints and exits, but an app that takes over the terminal and stays interactive until you quit.
